geometry_edits.rationale: Transform the current clip into a frontage notch so the dominant mass keeps continuity while opening a usable public edge.
Tie the notch to the verified access side in the program frame.
Create a clear but bounded public indentation at the ground.
Keep the carve shallow enough to preserve the dominant body and avoid over-clipping.
Tune the overall subtraction fraction so the public seam is evident in plan and section.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass across the four views, with a recognizable lifted/main body and a small secondary appendage. It is not collapsing into separate volumes, and it responds to the parcel better than a box-filler would. The strong point is the readable main silhouette; the weakness is the access-edge response: the blue frontage is acknowledged only indirectly, with no especially legible court, notch, or public seam at the ground. The mass also feels a bit thick and generic in section, so it supports neighborhood living plausibly, but not yet with the clarity of active threshold and public void expected by the brief. Overall this is a passable early mass with a coherent gesture, but it needs a cleaner access-facing carve or terrace to better align with the program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more explicitly cultural/pavilion-like and more refined in void articulation than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise community massing with a large central void and a legible bridge/connector can support an active neighborhood program without becoming a tower object.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger campus-like aggregation; could overstate fragmentation if copied literally.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced campus composition around a shared court can create hierarchy and public open-space structure at neighborhood scale.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More transparent and roof-driven than the candidate; avoid turning the body into a pure slab.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long, horizontal mass with a courtyard void and folded roof logic helps the program read as mixed-use and public-facing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Landscape-heavy and sectional; candidate currently under-delivers the clarity of the public terrace.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terrace/ribbon massing with bridging and a stepped public section can produce an inhabitable neighborhood gesture.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More articulated and multi-winged; candidate is simpler and should not be over-fragmented.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a central void with strong hierarchy and overhead connection reinforce mixed-use public life.

warnings: The access edge is not strongly activated; the response is closer to neutral than publicly legible.
Void logic exists but is weakly expressed as a true civic court or seam.
The section reads somewhat generic; a more explicit terrace/notch/courtyard would better support the brief.
